sample_unit: ED visits (MC-MED, Site A; simulated across 1,000 shifts)

links.outcome: Supervised model AUROC drop from development site to external site
links.effect: XGBoost AUROC fell from 0.892 to 0.807 on external data; BT-LLM-Enriched stayed stable (0.826 to 0.831) and was statistically indistinguishable from XGBoost externally.
links.quote: On external validation, supervised model performance attenuated (XGBoost AUROC 0.892 to 0.807) while BT-LLM-Enriched remained stable (0.826 to 0.831); the two were statistically indistinguishable on external data.

unlisted_practices: Pairwise LLM-judge comparisons aggregated with a Bradley-Terry model for ED waiting-room prioritization without site-specific training

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an LLM-based pairwise ranking model for emergency department triage across simulated shifts and external datasets, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
